writeup: Astronomers have identified a new eclipsing binary star system called TIC 133688675, which they believe could warrant further investigation. The system's two stars orbit each other every 2.8524 days, and when the primary star passes in front of its companion, Earth observers detect a 1.95% drop in brightness. The discovery emerged from automated analysis of telescope data, producing a strong detection signal of 71.7 and passing all data quality checks. Remarkably, this candidate had never appeared in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a genuinely novel discovery. However, the system's companion star does not show a detectable secondary eclipse, and the pipeline's machine-learning classifier assigned it a moderate confidence score of 0.33, suggesting further observations would help confirm its true nature.
